newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran cleric says Israelis deserve death for poster.
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric says Israelis deserve death for poster.

text.p: A senior Iranian cleric has said Israelis responsible for a poster depicting Islam's Prophet Mohammad as a pig should be killed and Moslem groups called for protests , Iran's media said on Thursday.

"Without a doubt all those elements involved in carrying out this offence are condemned to death and Moslems are dutybound to punish them for their deeds," Ayatollah Yousef Sanei said in a statement published by the Tehran daily Ettelaat.
"Whoever sacrifices his life along this path for Islam and its dear Prophet will reach the rank of martyrdom," Sanei said.
A senior cleric, Sanei is the brother of Ayatollah Hassan Sanei who heads a foundation which has offered a $2.5 million reward for the killing of British author Salman Rushdie.

Several Islamic groups and state-affiliated bodies called for nationwide demonstrations on Friday, the day when Shi'ites mark Mohammad's death, against the pasting of the posters in the West Bank town of Hebron desecrating the Prophet and the holy Koran, Tehran radio said.

Iranian officials and religious leaders have called for joint action by Islamic states against the desecration for which Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has issued an apology after renewed violent protests by Palestinians.
Israeli police have said they had arrested a 26-year-old Jewish woman suspected of pasting the posters on storefronts.

Rushdie has been in hiding since Iran's late leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini in 1989 issued a fatwa, or religious edict, calling for the Indian-born writer's death for alleged blasphemy against Mohammad and Islam in his novel "The Satanic Verses".
